title: Shishak (Shoshenq I)
lead: Shoshenq I, founder of Egypt's 22nd dynasty (about 945–924 BC), the first pharaoh the Bible names. He sheltered Jeroboam and invaded Judah and Israel in Rehoboam's fifth year, about 925 BC, a campaign recorded on the temple walls at Karnak.

sections.h: Shishak in the Bible and at Karnak
sections.b: Jeroboam fled to Shishak from Solomon (1 Kings 11:40). In Rehoboam's fifth year Shishak came up against Jerusalem and took the treasures of the temple and palace, including Solomon's gold shields (1 Kings 14:25–28). Chronicles adds 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen and troops from Libya and Cush, and a prophetic warning by Shemaiah (2 Chronicles 12:2–12). Shoshenq's victory relief beside the Bubastite Portal at Karnak lists about 150 towns, many in the Negev and in the northern kingdom; Jerusalem's name is not preserved. A fragment of his stele was found at Megiddo. Because Egyptian chronology dates his reign, the campaign is one of the anchors for dating the kings.
